key_insight: Dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Controlling detonation-spray deposition to minimize porosity can improve coating protection on Q235 steel, with wear performance dependent on operating humidity.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Assess droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and long-term corrosion behavior.
Test friction and wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links higher porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate with increasing humidity.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear trends involve Si3N4–water tribochemistry and may not generalize to other counterface materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
